summary: Sacred call (max 2 uses): every Red Button charm you have equipped needs 1 fewer charge to be ready again, permanently (never below 1).
tip: Pick it once your Red Button charms are on the table; charms bought later keep full cost. Ring Bell (3 to 2) and Midas Touch (4 to 3) then fire noticeably more often.

effects.text: Only Red Button charms equipped when you pick it get cheaper (minimum 1 charge); charms bought afterwards keep their normal charge cost.

synergies.why: Needs 2 charges instead of 3: +1 Symbols Multiplier every 2 Rounds instead of every 3.
Needs 3 charges instead of 4, so its permanent value Rounds come every 3 Rounds instead of 4.
Needs 4 charges instead of 5 (3 after a second pick), so its yellow retrigger Rounds come sooner.
At 1 charge it can flip every Round, gaining its Patterns Multiplier twice as fast.
The pick fires twice: 2 fewer charges on every equipped Red Button charm.
Discarding it later fires the call again for the Red Button charms you own by then.

assumptions: Assumed the cheaper cost stays with each charm even if it is moved to a drawer and back.
The engine applies the reduction to all Red Button charms, including ones bought later.

summary: Sacred call: gives every charm in the store a random Trait, then makes one of them free.
tip: Repeatable ticket saver: a free charm that also carries a Trait. Buy the cheap charms you want first so the free pick is likelier to land on a pricey one. Traits raise most other prices.

synergies.why: Every traited charm you equip adds +1 Patterns Multiplier.
Avid and Ambitious Traits rolled here become x2 multipliers.
Takes 1 ticket off the other charms, which the Traits made pricier.

assumptions: 'Modify' read as applying a random Trait (the wording later DLC cards use for Traits).
Assumed the free charm is chosen at random among the charms in the store.
Phone-applied random Traits are equally likely (wiki), so about 1 in 7 is Devious.

summary: Sacred call (once per run): every Pattern triggers one extra time for the rest of the run, doubling Pattern payouts.
tip: Take it on sight. Megaphone or Barathrum turn the single use into more permanent triggers, and the extra triggers also count for Pentacle, the Cats and other Pattern-count charms.

synergies.why: The one allowed pick fires twice: Patterns trigger 2 extra times for good.
Discarding it later adds a second permanent extra trigger.
Phone abilities trigger once more, so the pick gives +2 triggers.
Doubled Pattern counts make its 5+ Pattern growth spins far more common.
7+ Pattern spins become common, each paying double your Interest.
A doubled Jackpot spin is about 20 Patterns, past its 15+ trigger.

summary: Sacred call: spawns a random Sacred charm on your table (even past your slot limit), then halves the coins you are holding.
tip: Deposit or spend coins before answering to shrink the loss. Most Sacred charms trigger on 999s, so extra 666/999 odds (Devious Traits, Necronomicon) make them stronger.

synergies.why: Fires twice: two Sacred charms, though your coins are halved twice.
Discarding it later spawns another Sacred charm.
Phone abilities trigger once more: two Sacred charms per call.
In Sacred Mode its +3% 666 chance means more 999s for the Sacred charms.
The spawned Sacred charm arrives with a random Trait.

assumptions: Only coins in hand are halved, not deposited coins (per the wiki's strategy note).
Assumed effects that raise 666 odds raise 999 odds in Sacred Mode.

summary: Sacred call: doubles the current value of every small Pattern (3 or fewer Symbols: HOR, VER, DIAG and the 2-symbol ones).
tip: Best while small Patterns still pay most of your coins. It doubles current values, so take value adders first (I'm thinking of some strategies, Diesel Locomotive), then double.

synergies.why: Adds base value to the same small Patterns; take it first so the doubling includes it.
The 2-symbol Patterns it adds are small Patterns, so they are doubled too.
Grows every Pattern by its base value; doubling a grown value gains more.

summary: Sacred call: doubles the current value of every large Pattern (4+ Symbols: HOR-L, HOR-XL, ZIG, ZAG, ABOVE, BELOW, EYE, JACKPOT).
tip: Best in Luck and Jackpot builds, where big Patterns earn most of your coins. It doubles current values, so add first (I found a winning strategy) and stack it with I can't quit now.

synergies.why: Adds base value to the same large Patterns; take it first so the doubling includes it.
Doubles the Jackpot again: the two multiply.
Luck +7 on the last spin forms the big Patterns this doubles.
Forces Above or Below, both doubled by this call.
Forces Zig and Zag every 7 spins, both doubled by this call.
Its Above/Below doublings multiply with this one.

summary: The default Memory Card: no effects, a normal run.
tip: The neutral baseline. Use it to learn the game or when no other card fits your plan; every other card bends the rules for better or worse.

summary: Run-long: the store shows only 3 charms instead of 4, but every Deadline starts with 2 free Restocks.
tip: Free Restocks carry over: bank them for Shopping Cart (+2 Symbols Multiplier each) or spend them to grow Bell Pepper. Fewer store slots make Cigarettes rerolls worse.

effects.text: For the whole run the store has 3 charm slots instead of 4.

synergies.why: Each held free Restock is +2 Symbols Multiplier, and 2 more arrive every Deadline.
Each Restock spent this Deadline adds +2 to its Luck bonus.
Every Restock recharges a Red Button charm.
Doubles the free Restocks you are holding.

antiSynergies.why: With 3 slots its restock-and-reappear trick shows fewer new charms per buy.

assumptions: Free Restocks can be stockpiled between Deadlines (wiki strategy note).

summary: Run-long: 7 Rounds per Deadline but only 1 spin per Round; ending a Deadline early pays 2 tickets per skipped Round instead of 4.
tip: Each spin is both first and last of its Round: Hamsa and Rotated Hamsa fire every spin and Red Button charms recharge 7 times a Deadline. Cat Food brings you back to 3 spins per Round.

synergies.why: +2 spins per Round gives 21 spins per Deadline again.
Every spin is a Round's first, so all Patterns trigger twice on every spin.
Every spin is a Round's last, so every spin gets Luck +7.
Charges refill at every Round's end: 7 per Deadline instead of 3.
Interest pays at every Round's end, 7 times per Deadline instead of 3.

antiSynergies.why: Loses 5% per Round, so it lasts only 5 spins.
Breaks after 10 Rounds, which is only 10 spins.
Its doubling lasts until the Round ends, right after the spin that earned it.
Its Round-long Pattern bonus expires right after the spin that earned it.
Its 2 extra Rounds are only 2 spins.

assumptions: The 2-instead-of-4 skip reward is encoded as -2 tickets per skipped Round versus normal.
Assumed first-spin and last-spin effects both apply to a Round's single spin.

summary: Run-long: each Deadline is one Round of up to 21 spins that pays extra tickets. The run starts with 27 coins and 5 tickets.
tip: Round-long buffs now last the whole Deadline (Vine's Soup, Number 1, Midas Touch) and each extra Round is 21 spins. Interest and Red Button recharges come once a Deadline.

effects.text: The single Round pays more Clover Tickets than a normal Round (exact amount not stated).

synergies.why: An extra Round is 21 more spins.
Every extra Round it grants is a full 21-spin Round.
A doubling lasts the rest of the 21-spin Deadline.
One press retriggers yellow Patterns for the whole Deadline.
Fades 5% per Round, so its Repetition lasts 5 whole Deadlines.
Fades 5% per Round, so its Chain chance lasts 5 whole Deadlines.

antiSynergies.why: Fires on 1 spin per Deadline instead of 3.
Fires on 1 spin per Deadline instead of 3.
With 1 Round per Deadline there is nothing to skip.
No Rounds to skip, so it gains only +1 per Deadline.
No Rounds to skip, so its Golden chance never grows.
Interest pays once per Deadline instead of 3 times.

assumptions: The extra tickets per Round are not stated; likely sized to make up for the 2 missing Rounds.
Assumed effects lasting 'until the end of the Round' now last the whole Deadline.

summary: Start the run with 12 tickets, but Rounds pay 0 tickets for the rest of the run unless an effect changes it.
tip: A fast start: buy 3-4 charms right away. After that, tickets must come from skipped Rounds, selling charms, Florid Traits or Ticket modifiers such as Raging Capitalist.

synergies.why: Ticket modifiers on every Symbol replace the lost Round income.
A 2-ticket source of Ticket modifiers on Clovers.
Turns the 12-ticket start into more tickets at each Deadline's end.
30% of the debt at once helps you end Deadlines early for 4 tickets per skipped Round.
+5 tickets per call.

antiSynergies.why: Its growth needs phone rerolls, which cost tickets you no longer earn each Round.

assumptions: Assumed Deadline-end rewards (skipped Rounds, Florid, CloverPot) still pay; only the per-Round payout drops to 0.

summary: Run-long: every Deadline's debt is halved, but you start with only 15 coins, already deposited. Scores can't go to the Leaderboard.
tip: The relaxed-run card: halved debts are worth about double income all run. Expect a slow first Deadline from the tiny start, then it carries you.

effects.text: The run starts with only 15 coins, already deposited at the ATM. Runs with this card can't upload a score to the Leaderboard.

synergies.why: Halved debts are easier to pay early, so you skip more Rounds for its multiplier.
Halved debts make skipped Rounds common, and each one raises its Golden chance.
More skipped Rounds mean bigger Luck triggers next Deadline.

assumptions: '50% easier' read as every debt multiplied by 0.5 (the Hard Mode wiki page calls it a debt modifier).
Assumed the 15 deposited coins replace the usual starting coins.

summary: When a Deadline ends with 6+ charms equipped, one of them is discarded at random, then you get 2 free Restocks.
tip: A drawback card: any Deadline can cost you a key charm. Dung Beetle grows on each forced discard, Vorago can return the lost charm, and drawers let you drop to 5 charms first.

effects.text: When a Deadline ends with 6 or more charms equipped, one equipped charm is discarded at random (before the 2 free Restocks).

synergies.why: Each forced discard raises all Symbols by their base value.
Holds the discarded charm so you can bring it back.
Bank the 2 free Restocks for +4 Symbols Multiplier.
Pays coins whenever an effect discards a charm.

antiSynergies.why: Its slow Deadline-by-Deadline growth is lost if it is the charm picked.
Its stacked Symbols Multiplier can be wiped by a random discard.
Its banked Symbols Multiplier can be wiped by a random discard.

assumptions: Assumed the 2 free Restocks come only when the discard happens (6+ charms equipped).
Assumed only charms on the table count, not those in drawers.

summary: Run-long: every Deadline's debt is doubled. Escaping through the door unlocks a cosmetic Golden Knob for the slot machine.
tip: A pure challenge card: pick it only to chase the Golden Knob with a build you trust. Every target is twice as high, so permanent scaling matters even more.

effects.text: Opening the door (escaping) with this card unlocks the Golden Knob for the slot machine, if you don't have it yet.

assumptions: The Golden Knob is assumed to be cosmetic (it is tied to the 'Omnipotent' achievement).

summary: Run-long: choosing Most Spins doubles the 666 chance for that Round; choosing Fewer Spins halves it.
tip: From Deadline 3, take Fewer Spins on Rounds you can't afford to lose. Devil builds (Baphomet, Gabihbb'h) and Sacred runs, where the odds cover 999s, can welcome Most Spins.

effects.text: The x2 applies to Rounds played with the Most Spins option; picking Fewer Spins halves the 666 chance for that Round instead.

synergies.why: Doubled 666 odds double Above/Below more often.
More 666s mean more Rounds with a doubled Symbols Multiplier.
More 666s mean more Rounds with tripled gem values.
Cancels a 666 while it still counts for 666 charms.
In Sacred Mode, more 999s double your Patterns Multiplier more often.
In Sacred Mode, more 999s mean more forced Jackpots.

assumptions: The engine assumes Most Spins, so the 666 chance is encoded as doubled.
Assumed the same odds change applies to 999s in Sacred Mode.

summary: Run-long: 666s are twice as likely, but hitting a Jackpot refunds all coins lost to 666s earlier in that same Round.
tip: Only for Luck/Jackpot or devil builds: frequent Jackpots refund most losses, and 666 charms like Baphomet trigger twice as often. Holy Bible covers Rounds you can't lose.

effects.text: Whenever you hit a Jackpot, you get back all coins lost to 666s earlier in the same Round.

synergies.why: Twice the 666s means twice the Above/Below doublings.
More 666s mean more Rounds with a doubled Symbols Multiplier.
Its guaranteed Jackpot Round can refund a 666 hit earlier in that Round.
Luck +7 on the last spin raises the odds of a late, refunding Jackpot.
Cancels a 666 outright, a safety net against the doubled odds.

assumptions: Assumed the refund only covers 666 losses from before the Jackpot in the same Round.
Assumed 999 odds double in Sacred Mode as well.
